title: Mapped medium or heavy smoke captured 9-37% of elevated nearby PM2.5 dates in four US bird survey samples in 2011-2024
abstract: We tested mapped smoke against nearby daily surface PM2.5 in 10,734 accepted US bird survey runs in 2011-2024. Medium or heavy smoke captured 9-37% of dates above 12 micrograms per cubic metre in four East and West, early and late samples. Positive predictive value was 25-59%. A four-class calibration fitted in the early period gave no clear Brier score gain in the later period in either region. Only 55 monitored dates exceeded 35. Monitor coverage was 22-51% of eligible runs. The analysis reuses a verified campaign panel; it is not an independent biological replication. Total PM2.5 includes non-fire pollution, monitors can be 50 km away, and daily measures do not match dawn surveys. Few year clusters limit interval accuracy. These results limit a surface-pollution reading of prior bird-count null results. They do not estimate a bird effect or a causal climate effect. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact input hashes and verified retrieval instructions are included. Source record tables stay external.

display.caption: Medium or heavy HMS smoke versus nearby daily PM2.5 >12. Intervals use route and year clusters and a four-sample correction. Few year clusters limit coverage.
